comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that surprised me: Bolivia's 2009 constitution does not just gesture at indigenous languages, it names 36 of them one by one, including a few with almost no speakers left. Meanwhile in Paraguay, where Guarani has been level with Spanish since 1992, Guarani-only speakers fell from 28 in 100 to 12 in twenty years. Sources are listed in the description. Where you live, is a minority or indigenous language official on paper, and does it actually show up in schools, courts or forms?
